maml:description.maml:para: Connects to a Microsoft Dataverse environment.

The Connect-PSDataverse cmdlet establishes a connection to a Microsoft Dataverse environment using one of several authentication methods: connection string, client secret, certificate, managed identity, Isystem.AzAuth (-AuthMode, the same modes PSDataRepository uses, including WorkloadIdentity, NonInteractive, Interactive and DeviceCode with a named on-disk cache), or a delegated user sign-in with a portable in-memory token cache (-Delegated, for environments without application users). The connection is stored in the current PowerShell runspace and used by all subsequent Dataverse cmdlets.
A Dataverse connection string provided as a SecureString. Used in the ConnectionString parameter set.
The URL of the Dataverse environment (e.g., https://org.crm.dynamics.com).

The Microsoft Entra application (client) ID. Mandatory for ClientSecret and Certificate; optional for AzAuth (mode dependent) and Delegated, where it defaults to the well-known public Dataverse client 51f81489-12ee-4a9e-aaae-a2591f45987d.
The client secret for app-based authentication (ClientSecret set, or AzAuth -AuthMode ClientSecret), provided as a SecureString.
The thumbprint of the certificate used for certificate-based authentication (Certificate set, or AzAuth -AuthMode ClientCertificate).
The Microsoft Entra tenant ID. Optional; when omitted, delegated flows use the organizations authority.
Indicates that managed identity authentication should be used. Typically used when running in Azure.
The client ID of a user-assigned managed identity. If omitted, the system-assigned identity is used.
Maximum number of retry attempts for transient failures. Valid range: 0-10. Default: 3.
Pause in seconds between retry attempts. Valid range: 1-60. Default: 5.

Isystem.AzAuth authentication mode. Names match PSDataRepository -AuthMode: ClientSecret, ClientCertificate, ManagedIdentity, WorkloadIdentity, NonInteractive (Azure.Identity default chain), Interactive (browser), DeviceCode, Cache (silent from a named on-disk cache).
An X509Certificate2 instance for AzAuth ClientCertificate mode. Alternative to -CertificateThumbprint and -CertificatePath.
Path to a certificate file (PFX/PEM) for AzAuth ClientCertificate mode. Alternative to -CertificateThumbprint and -Certificate.

Delegated (user) sign-in with an in-memory MSAL token cache that the caller persists wherever it wants (Key Vault, file). Use when the environment has no application users, such as Dataverse for Teams without a premium licence. Export the cache with Get-PSDataverseTokenCache and pass it back through -TokenCache on the next run.
Federated token for AzAuth WorkloadIdentity mode (for example the AKS or GitHub Actions identity token), as a SecureString.

What to do when the token cache holds no usable refresh token: Auto (silent, then browser), Silent (fail - for unattended runs), Interactive (silent, then browser), DeviceCode (silent, then device-code prompt for headless hosts). Default: Auto.
Redirect URI of the public client application used by -Delegated. Default: http://localhost.
Timeout for interactive and managed-identity token acquisition in AzAuth modes. Valid range: 10-600. Default: 120.
Serialized token cache produced by Get-PSDataverseTokenCache in an earlier session. Seeds the in-memory MSAL cache so the sign-in is silent.
Name of the on-disk MSAL token cache used by AzAuth Interactive, DeviceCode and Cache modes. The cache is protected by DPAPI/keychain and bound to the current user and machine.
Account (UPN or object id) to select from the named cache in AzAuth Cache mode.
This cmdlet does not produce output.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets a Dataverse record by ID or alternate key.
The Get-PSDataverseRecord cmdlet retrieves a single record from a Dataverse table by its logical name and unique identifier. You can optionally specify which columns to retrieve.
The logical name of the Dataverse table (e.g., "account", "contact"). Used in the ByProperties parameter set.
The unique identifier (GUID) of the record to retrieve. Accepts pipeline input by value (e.g., raw Guid from New-PSDataverseRecord) or by property name. Used in the ByProperties parameter set.

An Entity object to re-retrieve. The LogicalName and Id are extracted from the entity. Used in the ByInputObject parameter set. Accepts pipeline input from Find-PSDataverseRecord or Invoke-PSDataverseFetchXml.
An array of column logical names to retrieve. If omitted, all columns are returned.
Alternate key (attribute name = value hashtable) identifying the record instead of -Id, e.g. @{ accountnumber = 'A-1' }.
The Dataverse record as an Entity object.

A hashtable of attribute-value pairs for equality filtering. Null values produce an "is null" condition.
A hashtable of attribute-value pairs for LIKE (wildcard) filtering. Use % as the wildcard character.
An array of column logical names to retrieve. If omitted, all columns are returned.
The logical name of the column to sort results by.
When specified with -OrderBy, sorts results in descending order.
Maximum number of records to return. Valid range: 1-5000. Default: 50. Ignored when -All is specified.
Retrieves all matching records across all pages. Overrides -Top.

maml:description.maml:para: Updates an existing Dataverse record, or upserts it by alternate key.

The Set-PSDataverseRecord cmdlet updates the specified attributes of an existing record in a Dataverse table, addressed by Id, by alternate -Key, or by a piped Entity. With -Upsert the record is created when it does not exist. Lookup attributes can be given as nested hashtables @{ LogicalName = ...; Id = ... } or @{ LogicalName = ...; Key = @{ ... } }. Failures are non-terminating errors, so a pipeline of records continues and -ErrorAction decides. This cmdlet supports ShouldProcess, so you can use -WhatIf and -Confirm.
The logical name of the Dataverse table containing the record. Used in the ByProperties parameter set.
The unique identifier (GUID) of the record to update. Used in the ByProperties parameter set.
An Entity object identifying the record to update. The LogicalName and Id are extracted from the entity. Used in the ByInputObject parameter set.
A hashtable of attribute logical names and their new values.
When specified, the cmdlet retrieves and returns the updated entity after the update operation.

Prompts for confirmation before updating the record.

Create the record when it does not exist (UpsertRequest). Outputs a DataverseUpsertResult with the record Id and RecordCreated; with -PassThru the full record is retrieved instead.

maml:description.maml:para: Executes a batch of Dataverse operations (create/update/upsert/delete).

The Invoke-PSDataverseBatch cmdlet sends multiple create, update, upsert, and delete operations to Dataverse in a single ExecuteMultiple request. Each operation is a hashtable with Action (Create, Update, Upsert, Delete), LogicalName, and Id or Key (alternate key hashtable) plus Attributes; lookups are written as nested hashtables @{ LogicalName = ...; Id = ... } or @{ LogicalName = ...; Key = @{ ... } }. The cmdlet returns a typed DataverseBatchResult with success and failure counts and one Items entry per operation (Index, Action, LogicalName, Id, Succeeded, RecordCreated, ErrorCode, Message). The cmdlet supports ShouldProcess with medium confirm impact.

An array of hashtables defining the operations. Each hashtable must contain: Action (Create/Update/Delete), LogicalName, and optionally Id (required for Update/Delete) and Attributes (a nested hashtable of column values).
When specified, the batch continues processing remaining operations even if one fails.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs without actually executing the batch.
Prompts for confirmation before executing the batch.
A typed object with TotalRequests, SuccessCount, FailureCount, IsFullSuccess, Items (per-operation outcome with the record Id, ErrorCode and Message) and optionally Errors.

maml:description.maml:para: Executes Dataverse operations in a single atomic transaction.

The Invoke-PSDataverseTransaction cmdlet sends multiple create, update, upsert, and delete operations to Dataverse as a single atomic transaction using ExecuteTransaction. If any operation fails, all operations are rolled back. Each operation is a hashtable with Action (Create, Update, Upsert, Delete), LogicalName, and Id or Key (alternate key hashtable) plus Attributes; lookups are written as nested hashtables @{ LogicalName = ...; Id = ... } or @{ LogicalName = ...; Key = @{ ... } }. The cmdlet supports ShouldProcess with medium confirm impact.

An array of hashtables defining the operations. Each hashtable must contain: Action (Create/Update/Delete), LogicalName, and optionally Id (required for Update/Delete) and Attributes (a nested hashtable of column values).
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs without actually executing the transaction.
Prompts for confirmation before executing the transaction.
The number of operations that were committed in the transaction.

maml:description.maml:para: Exports the delegated token cache of the current (or last) session.

The Get-PSDataverseTokenCache cmdlet returns the serialized MSAL token cache of a session opened with Connect-PSDataverse -Delegated, as one opaque string (prefix PSDVTC1: followed by base64). The refresh token lives inside that cache and MSAL may rotate it during a session, so persist the value after the work is done - to Azure Key Vault (for example through PSDataRepository), a file, or any other secret store - and pass it back through Connect-PSDataverse -TokenCache on the next run. The value stays available after Disconnect-PSDataverse until the next Connect-PSDataverse. Treat it as a credential.
The serialized token cache envelope.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets Dataverse table metadata: logical name, primary key and name columns, entity set.

Every other cmdlet takes the LOGICAL name of a table, which is neither the display name the maker portal shows nor the plural collection name. This cmdlet finds it, and tells the two causes of the SDK error "the entity with a name = X was not found in the MetadataCache" apart: the table is not in this environment, or the name is spelled differently. An exact name costs one metadata request; a wildcard has to read the whole catalogue, because the metadata service has no server-side name filter. Only custom tables are listed unless -IncludeSystem is given.
Include the tables that ship with the platform (~1,300 of them). Without it only custom tables - the ones with a publisher prefix - are listed.

Logical name of the table; wildcards are allowed (it3c_*). Omitted, every table is returned - custom ones only, unless -IncludeSystem is given. An exact name costs one metadata request; a wildcard reads the whole catalogue, because the metadata service has no server-side name filter.
Table metadata, so the output of Get-PSDataverseTable can be piped in by property name.
One object per table: logical name, display name, primary id and name columns, entity set name.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Lists every custom table whose logical name starts with the publisher prefix.
One table, without reading the catalogue: logical name, primary id and name columns, entity set name for Web API URLs.
Pipes each table into a query: the first five rows of every custom table. The table name binds by property name.
Row counts for every custom table. The primary id column travels with the object, so tables that break the {name}id convention are counted correctly.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets the columns of a Dataverse table, with their types and writability.

A retrieved record shows only the columns that have a value; this shows the table as it is defined. IsValidForCreate and IsValidForUpdate are worth reading before a mapping is blamed: calculated, rollup and system columns read perfectly well and are rejected on write. The table name is exact - use Get-PSDataverseTable to find it - while -Name filters the columns and accepts wildcards.
Only custom columns - the ones carrying a publisher prefix.
Logical name of the table. Exact, not a search: use Get-PSDataverseTable to find it, or pipe that cmdlet's output in.
Column name filter; wildcards are allowed (it3c_*). Omitted, every column of the table is returned.
Only columns that can be written on create or update. Calculated, rollup and system columns read perfectly well and are rejected on write, which is what this filters out.
Table metadata, so the output of Get-PSDataverseTable can be piped in by property name.
One object per column: logical name, type, required level, writability, length or lookup targets.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Every column of the table, sorted by logical name.
Only the custom columns that can actually be written - the set a mirror or an import may fill.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets the alternate keys of a Dataverse table and the state of their indexes.

Everything that upserts by key - Set-PSDataverseRecord -Key, an Upsert operation in Invoke-PSDataverseBatch - depends on a key whose index status is Active. A key whose index is Pending or Failed fails at runtime with a message that never mentions the index, which makes this the first thing to check when an upsert that worked yesterday stops working.
Logical name of the table. Exact; pipe Get-PSDataverseTable in to walk several.
Table metadata, so the output of Get-PSDataverseTable can be piped in by property name.
One object per alternate key: its columns and the state of its index.

dev:remarks.maml:para: The alternate keys of the table, their columns and index status.

command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Get-PSDataverseTable it3c_* | Get-PSDataverseKey | Where-Object IndexStatus -ne Active

dev:remarks.maml:para: Across every custom table, the keys that are not usable for an upsert yet.
